effect_favours.description: WHICH ARM the reported effect_size favours. The SIGN of a reported effect is not a reliable convention -- some papers report a raw measurement difference (a faster sprint TIME is a NEGATIVE number and a GOOD result) and others report it already oriented toward the treatment. State it explicitly so downstream never has to guess: 'ingredient' = the effect favours the study ingredient, 'control' = it favours the comparator, 'neither' = no meaningful difference. null when you cannot tell, which is always a valid answer.

effect_sd.description: The standard deviation of THIS endpoint, in the SAME unit as effect_size, when the paper PRINTS one (group means +/- SD, or a stated pooled SD). It is what lets a raw-unit difference (kg, watts, points) be standardised into a comparable effect. Only a printed SD -- never derive one from a standard error or a confidence interval. null when not printed.

effect_sd_basis.description: Which SD you reported: pooled across arms, the control arm's, the baseline SD, or unstated when the paper does not say.

contrast.description: Which comparison this claim reports: against an arm with no study ingredient (vs_ingredient_free), against another arm that ALSO received the ingredient (vs_ingredient_arm -- e.g. ingredient+X vs ingredient), a within-group pre/post change (within_group), or unclear.
